decisionGroups.title: VAT ID missing for a zero-rated EU customer
decisionGroups.why: You invoiced this customer without German VAT as an intra-EU supply. That is only allowed with a valid VAT ID. Without one, these invoices may owe 19 % VAT.

decisionGroups.title: A customer without a country
decisionGroups.why: The country decides whether German VAT applies. Some of this customer's invoices are in USD, which suggests they may not be in Germany.

decisionGroups.title: The same customer twice
decisionGroups.why: Answer this before the payments below: merging changes which customer an open item belongs to.

decisionGroups.title: Expense accounts the model was unsure about
decisionGroups.why: These decide which line of your profit and loss an expense appears on. Sorted by amount; invoices with the same description are grouped so you can answer them together.

decisionGroups.title: Payments we could not match to an invoice
decisionGroups.why: Money arrived and we don't know who paid it or for what. You can leave these open; they stay visible in the bank clearing account.

decisionGroups.title: Refunds without a credit note
decisionGroups.why: Money went out to a customer. Each should close one of your open credit notes.

decisionGroups.title: Customers who paid too much
decisionGroups.why: Small amounts. Keeping them as credit is the usual choice.

decisionGroups.title: A German customer's VAT ID looks wrong
decisionGroups.why: Their invoices carry German VAT, so the books are not affected. Worth fixing for the customer record.

decisionGroups.title: One-cent rounding differences
decisionGroups.why: The old system's gross amount was a cent off net plus VAT. Net plus VAT agrees with the VAT rate. Accept all in one go.

$comment: Copy of the default setup. Change words, people, roles and decision groups; no code changes needed. Run `npm test` to validate.
